title: Kneel
intro: Kneel takes wounded pride into a fantasy of absolute hierarchy. The speaker claims to have raised the opponent, converts that care into ownership and demands bodily submission. Every possible appeal—crying, begging, asking for comfort—is denied in advance, while his own moods become the only rule. The cooking brands and sound-games make the excess grotesquely ordinary. This is a dominating persona the song stages, not a moral authority the listener has to accept. Its force includes how completely it reverses the vulnerability heard elsewhere on the album.
reading: Care converted to ownership; arbitrary power refuses the forms of vulnerability the album elsewhere asks us to recognise.

revisions.editorial-32-raised-dog: Having raised someone with his own hands becomes a claim to own their obedience. The grievance is therefore more possessive than a simple demand for gratitude. Care is retrospectively recast as an investment whose return can be forced from the other person's body. The ancestor and grandson insults enlarge the same hierarchy: the opponent is not allowed to meet him as an equal, whatever their actual relationship.
revisions.32-phrase-dribble: The head underfoot slides into dribbling a ball and the claim that life is a game. The motivational 'I will not give up' now serves a scene of humiliation, rather than an admirable struggle by itself. This is one of the track's sharpest changes of moral context: persistence sounds different when the activity being sustained is domination. The sporting metaphor makes that control feel routine and repeatable.
revisions.editorial-32-throat-threat: The promise that nobody will answer a ruined throat reverses 'Throat', where an unheard performer describes pain and asks for care. Here the speaker imagines controlling the refusal himself. The connection need not establish a deliberate sequel to be illuminating: the same bodily vulnerability can be pleaded from one position and exploited from another. The album's different voices do not all occupy the same ethical ground.
revisions.editorial-32-safety-mood: A safety mechanism becomes dependent on how he happens to feel. That is the clearest statement of the power fantasy: no stable rule lets the other person know how to avoid punishment. The refusal of advice and unstoppable accelerator extend it. The exaggerated persona does not merely want a grievance settled; it wants freedom from limits while imposing total limits on somebody else.
